stem: When educating the family of a pediatric kidney transplant recipient with early post-transplant oliguria, which teaching point about acute tubular necrosis (ATN) aligns with standard references?

options.text: Children with ATN may present with oliguria before becoming anuric, and hyperkalemia can develop rapidly
Pediatric ATN always presents with immediate anuria without an oliguric phase
Serum potassium monitoring is unnecessary during pediatric ATN
ATN in children never requires dialysis therapy

explanation.rationale_correct: Pediatric kidney recipients with ATN may present with oliguria before anuria; close potassium monitoring is vital because anuric patients quickly become hyperkalemic and may require dialysis.

rationale_incorrect.B: Standard references describe oliguria preceding anuria in children with ATN rather than immediate anuria in every case.
rationale_incorrect.C: Close observation of serum potassium is specifically emphasized during pediatric ATN.
rationale_incorrect.D: Dialysis therapy may be required during ATN when renal failure persists.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 17, Pediatric Transplantation → kidney early complications → ATN → v.–vii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Children with ATN present with oliguria prior to becoming anuric … Close observation of serum potassium levels … Dialysis therapy is required

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 17 → kidney early complications → ATN → v.–vii. (pediatric oliguria before anuria, hyperkalemia monitoring, dialysis); PDF p. 901 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Pediatric ATN teaching angle distinct from adult primary-nonfunction risk combo (cctc-1054) and pre-emptive transplant benefit (cctc-1042); anchor verified on Cupples p. 901.

stem: When educating an intestinal transplant recipient about graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), which counseling point aligns with standard references?

options.text: GVHD incidence is highest in intestine transplant recipients compared with other solid-organ transplants
GVHD occurs only after bone marrow transplantation and never after solid-organ transplant
Intestinal transplant recipients have the lowest GVHD risk among solid-organ recipients
GVHD always resolves without morbidity after intestine transplantation

explanation.rationale_correct: Although GVHD is rare in solid-organ transplantation, incidence is highest in intestine recipients—approximately five to ten times higher than other solid organs—because of abundant lymphoid tissue in the graft.

rationale_incorrect.B: GVHD is common after bone marrow transplantation but can also occur, rarely, after solid-organ transplantation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Intestine recipients have the highest, not lowest, GVHD incidence among solid-organ transplants.
rationale_incorrect.D: GVHD after intestine transplant leads to significant morbidity and mortality in affected patients.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 13, Intestine Transplantation → 8. Graft-versus-host disease → b.–c.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Incidence is highest in intestine transplant recipients … 5 to 10 times higher … significant morbidity and mortality

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 13 → 8. Graft-versus-host disease → b.–c. (highest incidence in intestine recipients; morbidity/mortality); PDF p. 729 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

stem: When educating a heart transplant candidate about long-term allograft complications, how is coronary artery vasculopathy (CAV) classified in standard references?

options.text: A form of chronic graft rejection
An expected benign finding unrelated to rejection
A complication limited to the donor procurement phase only

explanation.rationale_correct: Coronary artery vasculopathy is thought to be a form of chronic graft rejection and is a major long-term complication affecting heart allografts.

rationale_incorrect.B: Hyperacute rejection occurs immediately after implantation and is distinct from the chronic vasculopathy process.
rationale_incorrect.C: CAV is a clinically significant chronic allograft complication rather than a benign expected finding.
rationale_incorrect.D: CAV develops in the transplanted heart over time rather than being confined to procurement.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Coronary artery vasculopathy is thought to be a form of: chronic graft rejection

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 9 → Study Questions → 23. (CAV as chronic graft rejection); PDF p. 506 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Heart CAV classification angle distinct from heart lifting restrictions (cctc-1059) and lifestyle combo (cctc-1060); anchor verified on Cupples p. 506.

stem: A coordinator is revising cytomegalovirus (CMV) prevention teaching for solid-organ recipients. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Universal prophylaxis gives antiviral therapy for a defined period to patients who are donor and/or recipient CMV IgG seropositive.
Preemptive therapy monitors patients intensively and treats CMV only after infection is detected.
CMV is never a cause of morbidity or mortality in solid-organ transplant recipients.
CMV prevention strategies vary by transplanted organ, program protocol, and donor–recipient serostatus.

explanation.rationale_correct: Standard references describe universal prophylaxis for seropositive donor and/or recipient pairs, preemptive therapy after surveillance detection, and program-specific strategies based on organ and serostatus. CMV is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, so statement III is false.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also correct—prevention strategies are organ- and serostatus-specific.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statements I and II are also true; statement III is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false; CMV is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in transplant recipients.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 4, Pharmacology → 4. Antiviral therapy → c. Strategies
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Universal prophylaxis … donor CMV IgG seropositive and/or recipient CMV IgG seropositive … Preemptive therapy … major cause of morbidity and mortality … specific to the transplanted organ … serostatus

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 4 → 4. Antiviral therapy → c. Strategies (universal prophylaxis, preemptive therapy, organ/serostatus-specific prevention); PDF p. 159 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).
